required_facts_checked: An AI Engineer integrates AI into a product and keeps the system reliable, evaluated, maintained and improved.
The role translates product requirements into scoped AI problems and selects and integrates appropriate foundation models and tools.
Prompt versioning, success metrics, comprehensive tests, deployment, monitoring, cost optimization and security are included.
AI Engineering overlaps with data science and ML engineering but often uses third-party foundation models through APIs such as OpenAI, Anthropic or Google.
Established ML teams may distribute AI work among data scientists, ML engineers and software engineers, increasing existing workload.
Dedicated AI Engineers may sit in product engineering, a centralized AI platform group or an applied ML team.
Startups often use a product-focused generalist who moves from experimentation to production hardening.
RAG includes ingesting source data, chunking, embeddings, semantic search and grounded response generation.
Agentic systems include function calling, structured tools, MCP and reasoning flows for tool use.
Evaluation includes real-input tests, structured-output checks, datasets, quality metrics and reruns after prompt or model updates.
Observability includes logging inputs and outputs, tracking errors and failures, dashboards and log analysis for quality drift.
The accompanying example progresses from a simple AI feature in an online classifieds site to RAG and agentic systems.
